# Code of Conduct

yup is a community of people building software together. We want everyone to feel welcome and safe here, whatever their background, identity, or level of experience.

## Our pledge

We, as contributors and maintainers, pledge to make participation in yup a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, caste, color, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

We pledge to act in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.

## Expected behavior

- Be kind and patient, especially with newcomers.
- Respect different opinions, viewpoints, and experiences.
- Give constructive feedback, and accept it gracefully.
- Take responsibility for your mistakes, apologize to those affected, and learn from them.
- Focus on what's best for the community, not just for yourself.

## Unacceptable behavior

- Sexualized language or imagery, and unwelcome sexual attention or advances of any kind.
- Trolling, insults, derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks.
- Harassment, in public or in private.
- Publishing someone's private information, such as a physical or email address, without their explicit permission.
- Any other conduct that would reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting.

## Scope

This code applies in all yup spaces, including issues, pull requests, discussions, chat channels, and events. It also applies when you officially represent yup in public, such as when using an official account or speaking at an event on the project's behalf.

## Reporting

If you experience or witness unacceptable behavior, report it to the maintainers at [support@yup.audio](mailto:support@yup.audio).

Every report will be reviewed promptly and fairly. Maintainers will respect the privacy and safety of the person who reported the incident.

## Enforcement

Maintainers may remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, issues, and other contributions that violate this code. They will explain moderation decisions when appropriate.

Maintainers will use these guidelines to decide on consequences:

| Level | Behavior | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Correction** | Inappropriate language or other behavior that is unprofessional or unwelcome. | A private, written warning explaining the problem. A public apology may be requested. |
| **2. Warning** | A single serious incident or a series of smaller ones. | A warning with consequences for continued behavior. No interaction with the people involved for a set period. |
| **3. Temporary ban** | A serious violation, including sustained inappropriate behavior. | A temporary ban from all interaction and communication with the community. |
| **4. Permanent ban** | A pattern of violations, harassment of an individual, or aggression toward or disparagement of groups of people. | A permanent ban from all public interaction within the community. |

Maintainers who don't follow or enforce this code in good faith may face consequences decided by other project leaders.
